idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of about 18%. Its v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging. We rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that had been healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

**Rollback**
- **Before:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Target:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. The build released before v2.3.1, v2.3.1-rc, only ran in staging and was unhealthy there too.
- **After:** All three regions are on v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Approval:** None was needed. v2.3.0 has already been healthy in production, so the change-manager rule for never-healthy versions doesn't apply.

**Incident**
- I opened INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api), which paged on-call. It describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery, and says the cause of the v2.3.1 failure should be found before it's redeployed.
- My first attempt to create it timed out. The incident list was still empty afterwards, so I sent the same request again with a key that prevents duplicates. Exactly one incident exists, so on-call was paged once.
